newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks advance in early morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks advance in early morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks fluctuated in early Monday morning trade, opening sharply lower on a sell off of property developer shares before trending marginally stronger, brokers said.
"Properties are under short-term selling pressure, said Adrian Ngan, director of Peregrine Securities.
The Hang Seng Index was 27 points down at 13,219, bouncing off a low of 13,103.94. Turnover was a robust HK$2.40 billion after 40 minutes of trade.
Ngan said the market was nervously awaiting more information on whether the government may adopt methods to dampen speculation in real estate market
Brokers also said stronger-than-expected economic figures coming from the U.S. would hold the local market to a fairly cautious pattern for the next two weeks.
"People are still showing a bit of caution following the bond market's reaction to the unemployment figures, said Francis Wong, executive director of DBS Securities.

The U.S. Labour Department reported non-farm payrolls had expanded by 262,000 jobs in December, compared with an expected 200,000. The price of the benchmark U.S. 30-year bond fell, giving a yield of 6.90 percent before closing at 95-19/32, down 1-6/32 to yield 6.85 percent.
Wong said he thought the index was likely to trade in a range between 13,000 and 13,400 in the next two week, then return to its uptrend at end of January.
"We'll see a seesaw pattern until we resume the rally at the end of the month, Wong added.
The January Hang Seng Index futures was trading 37 points up at 13,205 and the February contract put on 57 points to 13,275.
The property subindex trailed the market, down 0.27, compared with the index's 0.28 percent gain.
Developers Henderson Land and Sun Hung Kai Properties both shed HK$0.75 to HK$71.50 and HK$90.75. Great Eagle, which will report earnings for 1996 on Wednesday, added HK$0.10 to HK32.90.

The commercial and industrial sector, despite its heavy exposure to property earnings, led the market's modest advance. CITIC Pacific recovered HK$0.50 to HK$40.00 and Swire A added HK$0.50 to HK$71.25.
Hutchison Whampoa advanced HK$0.50 to HK$57.25. Brokers said institutions continued to favour Hutchison over Cheung Kong. The parent was unchanged at HK$71.25.
